findings.reviewed_statement: Adults 19+ women 1.1 mg/day; men 1.2 mg/day for vitamin B6.
findings.comparator: Adults 19-50: 1.3 mg/day; age 51+ differs by sex.
findings.recommendation: Use age-specific current vitamin B6 reference values.
Replace the older generalized target with current age/sex-specific reference values and retain clinical caveats.

findings.reviewed_statement: Nuts, seeds and legumes: 3 servings per day.
findings.comparator: At 2,000 calories, DASH lists 4-5 servings per week.
At 2,000 calories, lean meats, poultry and fish are 6 oz or less per day.
findings.recommendation: Express the DASH amount as a daily total tied to calorie level.

findings.reviewed_statement: Vegetable oil appears under foods to avoid.
findings.comparator: DASH includes vegetable oils; at 2,000 calories fats and oils are 2-3 servings/day.
findings.recommendation: Remove vegetable oil from a blanket avoid category and distinguish unsaturated oils from saturated-fat sources.

findings.reviewed_statement: Buy foods with 5 ingredients or less.
findings.comparator: Ingredient count is not itself a federal nutrition-quality or processing classification.
findings.recommendation: Teach ingredient composition and Nutrition Facts interpretation rather than a hard ingredient-count cutoff.

findings.reviewed_statement: Saturated fat is grouped as healthy while polyunsaturated fat is grouped as unhealthy.
findings.comparator: AHA recommends monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats in place of saturated and trans fats.
findings.recommendation: Rebuild the fat taxonomy around unsaturated fats to emphasize, saturated fats to limit, and industrial trans fats to avoid.

findings.reviewed_statement: Omega-3 is listed as healthy while polyunsaturated fat is listed as unhealthy.
findings.comparator: Omega-3 fatty acids are polyunsaturated fats.
findings.recommendation: Nest omega-3 under polyunsaturated fats and remove the internal contradiction.

findings.reviewed_statement: Corn, soybean, sunflower and safflower oils are categorized as unhealthy.
findings.comparator: AHA lists these nontropical liquid plant oils among healthier choices compared with solid/saturated fats.
findings.recommendation: Do not classify regular polyunsaturated liquid plant oils as unhealthy solely because they are polyunsaturated.
